subject: sleep chronotypes

hook.say: You're not lazy and you're not undisciplined. You're one of four chronotypes.

types.name: The Lion
types.say: Up before the alarm, sharp by nine, completely useless by eight at night.

types.name: The Bear
types.say: You follow the sun. Most of the working world is built for you.

types.name: The Wolf
types.say: Your best thinking happens when everyone else is asleep.

types.name: The Dolphin
types.say: Light sleeper, alert mind, tired all day. The unlucky one.

kicker.say: Stop fighting your clock. Put the hard thing at your peak, not your morning.

caption: Being a wolf in a nine to five world isn't a character flaw. It's a scheduling problem.

subject: how you rest

hook.say: There are four ways to rest. Three of them aren't actually rest.

types.name: The Collapse
types.say: You lie down and scroll until the day is over. That's not rest, that's shutdown.

types.name: Productive Rest
types.say: You call it rest but there's a list involved.

types.name: Guilty Rest
types.say: You're horizontal and still doing maths about what you should be doing.

types.name: Actual Rest
types.say: Nothing is being achieved. That is the entire point.

kicker.say: Rest isn't a reward for finishing. It's part of the work.

caption: If your rest needs to be earned, you'll never get enough of it.

subject: bad days

hook.say: A bad day hits four kinds of people in four different places.

types.name: The Numb
types.say: You go flat. Nothing hurts and nothing lands.

types.name: The Fixer
types.say: You start solving. If there's a problem, there's a task.

types.name: The Talker
types.say: You need to say it out loud to one person. Then it shrinks.

types.name: The Spiral
types.say: One thing goes wrong and your brain writes an entire future about it.

kicker.say: You don't need a better day. You need the right kind of help.

caption: The spiral feels like planning. That's what makes it convincing.

subject: types of tired

hook.say: There are four kinds of tired, and sleep only fixes one of them.

types.name: Physical
types.say: Your body is heavy. Sleep actually works on this one.

types.name: Mental
types.say: You've made too many decisions today. Your brain is buffering.

types.name: Emotional
types.say: Nothing is wrong, and everything is too much.

types.name: Social
types.say: You like people. You just can't do one more conversation today.

kicker.say: If sleep isn't fixing it, it was never a sleep problem.

caption: You can sleep eight hours and still be exhausted. That's the difference between tired and depleted.

subject: phones at night

hook.say: What you do with your phone in bed says a lot about how you sleep.

types.name: The Scroller
types.say: One more video. That was forty minutes ago.

types.name: The Sleeper
types.say: Something is playing. You'll never know how it ends.

types.name: The Doom
types.say: You're not enjoying it. You're just not stopping.

types.name: The Airplane
types.say: Phone across the room. The alarm still works, weirdly.

kicker.say: The last thing you look at is what your brain works on all night.

caption: You don't have a sleep problem. You have a last hour problem.

subject: the first hour awake

hook.say: How you spend the first hour awake decides the next fifteen.

types.name: The Phone
types.say: Someone else's morning sets the tone for yours.

types.name: The Recovery
types.say: Water, light, no input. You're slow and it works.

types.name: The Planner
types.say: You write the day down before you live it.

types.name: The Chaos
types.say: You wake up already late and negotiate with the clock.

kicker.say: You don't need a five a m routine. You need ten minutes that belong to you.

caption: The first thing you touch in the morning is usually the thing that decides your mood.
